data.name: Elam
data.gender_notes: Elam is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Elam is derived from the ancient civilization in southwestern Iran, known as Elamites. It is believed to be derived from the word 'ilamu' in the Elamite language, meaning 'opposite' or 'foreign'. In the Bible, Elam is mentioned as a son of Shem and the ancestor of several important Elamite kings. Elamites were known for their rich cultural heritage and strong military prowess.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of foreignness, otherness, and exploration.
data.etymology: Elam belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Elamite, or from Elam.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Elam total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: עֵלָם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עֵלָם הוא שם הנגזר משורש ע־ל־מ, שפירושו 'להעלות' או 'להרים'. השם עֵלָם מופיע במקרא כשם בנו של שׁאול, מלך ישראל, וכשם אזור גיאוגרפי. הוא קשור לנושא של עלייה וגדילה.

in_greek.name: Ἠλάμ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἠλάμ ἦν περιοχή στὴν ἀρχαία Περσία, καὶ ὁ Ἠλάμ ἦταν υἱὸς τοῦ Σαούλ, βασιλέως τοῦ Ισραήλ. Τὸ ὄνομα Ἠλάμ συνδέεται μὲ τὴν ἰδέα τῆς ὑψώσεως καὶ τῆς ἀνυψώσεως.

in_english.name: Elam
in_english.meaning: Elam means a region or land elevated or uplifted
in_english.long_meaning: Elam originates from the Hebrew root 'ע־ל־מ' meaning 'to rise' or 'to be elevated'. It appears in the Bible as the name of a son of Shem and a region in ancient Persia. The name Elam signifies elevation, ascension, or a place of high ground. It carries spiritual connotations of rising above challenges and achieving greatness through faith and perseverance.

data.cultural_impact: The Elamites were a significant ancient civilization, which played a crucial role in the development of the Middle East. They established a powerful and influential empire, which lasted from around 3200 BCE to 539 BCE. Elamites were known for their artistic, architectural, and cultural achievements, which include the development of the cuneiform script, the first writing system in the world. The Elamites also made significant contributions to the development of ancient Iranian art and influenced the art and culture of Babylonia, Assyria, and other ancient civilizations in the region.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Elam holds great significance for Christians as it is mentioned in the Bible as the birthplace of King Zedekiah, the last Judean king before the Babylonian captivity. Elam is also mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the places to which the returning exiles travelled after the Babylonian conquest. In the New Testament, Elam is mentioned as the birthplace of one of the Magi or Wise Men who visited the infant Jesus, emphasizing the universality of the Christian message. Thus, the name Elam carries a spiritual significance for Christians as a reminder of the ancient Israelite connection to the Middle East and the broader world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Elam represents the descendants of Elam, a grandson of Shem and the eponymous ancestor of the Elamites, an ancient civilization in southwestern Iran. It symbolizes the call to embrace one's heritage and roots, fostering a deep sense of identity and connection to one's past.

biblical_reference.note: Elam was a son of Shem and a region in ancient Mesopotamia.

historical_references.reference: Elam is an ancient region in southwestern Iran, named after its original inhabitants, the Elamites. Elam was one of the first civilizations in Iran, dating back to at least 3500 BCE, and was known for its advanced urban planning, agriculture, and pottery making. It is believed that the Elamites adopted Zoroastrianism as their state religion around 1000 BCE.

During the Persian Empire, Elam became a satrapy (a province) under the rule of the Achaemenids. Elam was significant in Persian history as the site of several important battles, including the Battle of Halys in 585 BCE and the Battle of Cunaxa in 401 BCE. These battles marked the end of the Median Empire and the rise of the Persian Empire under Xerxes I.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Elam' has modern relevance in various contexts including ancestry tracing and historical research, as it refers to an ancient civilization in southwestern Iran. In the realm of geopolitics, Elam is mentioned as the historical name of the province of Khuzestan in Iran. Today, the name is also used as a surname in different parts of the world. On genealogy websites like MyHeritage and Ancestry.com, people search for their Elamite ancestors, while on Wikipedia, researchers delve into the history of Elam to understand the roots of various modern-day cultures and civilizations.
